statement.p: Consider the concentration, C, in mg per liter (L), of a drug in the blood as a function of x, the amount, in mg, of the drug given and t, the time in hours since the injection. For 0 \leq x \leq 4 and t \geq 0, we have C = f(x,t) = t e^{-t(5-x)}.

p.em: Be sure you can interpret what your answer means in terms of drug concentration, time and initial amount.

static.solution: f(3,1.5) = 1.5\,e^{-1.5(5-3)} = 0.0746806\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut mg}{\rm\mathstrut L}}. We see that 1.5 hours after the injection of 3 mg of this drug, the concentration of the drug in the blood is 0.0746806\ {\textstyle\frac{\rm\mathstrut mg}{\rm\mathstrut L}}.
